**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

# Todo

This file contains near term tasks with a short description
and reference links to more details.

Intro paragraphs in `## Todo` and `## Bugs` should begin every
line with 1 leading space so they don't match the `^\d+\. `
pattern that locates numbered entries; 2 or 3 spaces also work.

## In Progress

When a `## Todo` item is picked up, its text **moves** here
(never copied; one home per text). The picked-up task is a
`###` heading; a multi-cycle program adds one level, where the
program is the `###` and its current stage a `####` (headings
give the current work durable anchors, which numbered Todo
entries can't). The problem overview is followed by the
"plan", a bulleted list of the development "ladder". Each
rung is prepended with its commit reference, a literal
`[[N]]` placeholder until the commit is pushed, then
backfilled to a real file-local `[[n]]` ref (same pattern as
the chores As-built rungs):
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y-0 blah (done)
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y-1 blah blah (current)
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y-2 blah blah blah
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y close-out and validation

### Refactor: typed jj facade -> jj-lib in-process; end subprocess spawning

Version-control operations were ~30 hand-rolled `run("jj", ...)`
spawns plus every mutation, with per-module private wrappers
and raw-git vestiges in init: stderr parsing instead of typed
errors, and jj's single-attempt index-lock acquisition (the
push `bookmark-set` lock race in [bugs.md](notes/bugs.md))
can't be retried where it fails. A multi-ladder program; the
staged plan, design detail, and the eight absorbed former
Todos live in
[refactor-20260716.md](notes/refactor-20260716.md).

Program ladder in **straight trunk order**, one bullet per
commit that lands on the branch, so reading it top to bottom
is reading `git log --first-parent`. `refactor:` entries are
the program's rungs, one per cycle (adjacent stages
consolidated 2026-07-24; titles are the anticipated close-out
titles; unshipped versions are provisional, since jj-lib may
split into two cycles). `docs:` entries are interludes that
sit between cycles and belong to no rung. Every shipped ref
points at a close-out commit on `refactor-vc-x1`, treated as
permanent: the branch is long-lived and lands on main
merge-only, never rebased.

The order is load-bearing: a
trapezoid's `<base>` is the parent of its own first rung, not
the previous close-out, so 0.78.0 bases on 0.77.4. Taking the
close-out instead swallows the interludes into the merge's
ladder side, which already bit at 0.76.0, whose base was the
0.75.1 interlude. See
[the recipe](notes/cycle-protocol.md#trapezoid-close-out-recipe).

1	# Code conventions
2	
3	Conventions for source code. Read this before writing code. The Rust-specific sections apply
4	wherever the medium is a Rust crate (see [custom.md](../custom.md) for the project's medium).
5	
6	Universal file, pinned to vc-x1-work-repo-template; do not edit here. Project overrides go in
7	[custom.md](../custom.md).
8	
9	## Line width
10	
11	Source lines, including doc comments and inline comments, wrap at <=100 cols (rustfmt's
12	default `max_width`; the per-commit flow's `cargo fmt` enforces it for code, and the same limit
13	applies to the comment text it doesn't reflow).
14	
15	## Doc comments on every file, function, and method
16	
17	Every `.rs` file must begin with a `//!` module docstring. Every function and method must have
18	a `///` doc comment. Keep them brief: one sentence of purpose is often enough; the discipline
19	is that the comment exists, not that it be long. Doc comments follow the
20	[Prose form](prose.md#prose-form) shape (intro + bullets).
21	
22	This is a deliberate override of the generic "write no comments" default that applies to
23	inline `//` comments. Doc comments on the module / item surface are expected; inline
24	explanatory comments inside function bodies remain discouraged unless they capture a
25	non-obvious WHY.
26	
27	**Clap-derive args:** doc comments on `#[arg(...)]` fields drive `--help` output. Clap reflows
28	by default and collapses bullets into running prose. Add `#[arg(verbatim_doc_comment, ...)]` on
29	any field whose doc comment uses bullets so each `- ...` lands on its own line in the rendered
30	help.
31	
32	## `// OK: ...` comments on `unwrap*` calls (Rust)
33	
34	The default in non-test code is to **not** use `.unwrap()`, `.expect(...)`, or the
35	`.unwrap_or*(...)` siblings. Prefer a shape that doesn't need them (`match`, `if let`, slice
36	patterns, infallible-by-construction APIs), which is usually also the clearer code. This is a
37	lean, not a ban: some sites are legitimately best expressed with one. Two kinds of risk, both
38	in scope:
39	
40	- `.unwrap()` / `.expect(...)`: a panic path.
41	- `.unwrap_or(...)` / `.unwrap_or_default()` / `.unwrap_or_else(...)`: no panic, but a
42	  silently substituted value that can hide a wrong result.
43	
44	When one is used, three obligations attach:
45	
46	- A trailing `// OK: ...` comment justifying why the call is acceptable:
47	  - `// OK: <specific reason>`: document the real precondition, invariant, or domain reason.
48	    Preferred whenever the reason isn't self-evident.
49	  - `// OK: obvious`: the default is self-evident from context (e.g.
50	    `desc.lines().next().unwrap_or("")`, where an empty desc gives an empty title).
51	  - Bare `// OK` is not used (reads like a truncated comment). Abbreviations (e.g. `SE`) are
52	    not used because they require a decoder ring for readers seeing the code out of context.
53	- **Alert the user in conversation** when introducing one, so the site gets reviewed and
54	  appropriate uses are learned. Don't let it ride in silently on a larger diff.
55	- For `.unwrap()` / `.expect(...)`, an `#[allow(...)]` at the site, because Rust projects
56	  enable the project-wide lints in `Cargo.toml`:
57	
58	  ```toml
59	  [lints.clippy]
60	  unwrap_used = "warn"
61	  expect_used = "warn"
62	  ```
63	
64	  Every panicking site is then opt-in and visible in the diff; clippy (in the per-commit flow)
65	  catches any that slip through. The `_or*` siblings have no clippy lint; they are covered by
66	  the comment convention and the conversational alert. (The vc-x1-work-repo-template's
67	  `CargoRust.toml` seeds a base `Cargo.toml` with this section already in place.)
68	
69	```rust
70	let max = stderr_level.unwrap_or(LevelFilter::Info); // OK: default verbosity when -v/-vv absent
71	let first_line = desc.lines().next().unwrap_or("");  // OK: obvious
72	
73	match matches.len() {
74	    1 => {
75	        #[allow(clippy::unwrap_used)]
76	        // OK: `1 =>` arm guarantees matches.len() == 1
77	        Ok(TitleMatch::One(matches.into_iter().next().unwrap()))
78	    }
79	    // ...
80	}
81	```
82	
83	Tests (`#[cfg(test)]`) are exempt, since panicking on setup failure is the correct test
84	behavior.

wherever the medium is a Rust crate (see [custom.md](../custom.md) for the project's medium).

Universal file, pinned to vc-x1-work-repo-template; do not edit here. Project overrides go in
[custom.md](../custom.md).

## Line width

Source lines, including doc comments and inline comments, wrap at <=100 cols (rustfmt's
default `max_width`; the per-commit flow's `cargo fmt` enforces it for code, and the same limit
applies to the comment text it doesn't reflow).

## Doc comments on every file, function, and method

Every `.rs` file must begin with a `//!` module docstring. Every function and method must have
a `///` doc comment. Keep them brief: one sentence of purpose is often enough; the discipline
is that the comment exists, not that it be long. Doc comments follow the
[Prose form](prose.md#prose-form) shape (intro + bullets).

This is a deliberate override of the generic "write no comments" default that applies to
inline `//` comments. Doc comments on the module / item surface are expected; inline
explanatory comments inside function bodies remain discouraged unless they capture a
non-obvious WHY.

**Clap-derive args:** doc comments on `#[arg(...)]` fields drive `--help` output. Clap reflows
by default and collapses bullets into running prose. Add `#[arg(verbatim_doc_comment, ...)]` on
any field whose doc comment uses bullets so each `- ...` lands on its own line in the rendered
help.

## `// OK: ...` comments on `unwrap*` calls (Rust)

The default in non-test code is to **not** use `.unwrap()`, `.expect(...)`, or the
`.unwrap_or*(...)` siblings. Prefer a shape that doesn't need them (`match`, `if let`, slice
patterns, infallible-by-construction APIs), which is usually also the clearer code. This is a
lean, not a ban: some sites are legitimately best expressed with one. Two kinds of risk, both
in scope:

- `.unwrap()` / `.expect(...)`: a panic path.
- `.unwrap_or(...)` / `.unwrap_or_default()` / `.unwrap_or_else(...)`: no panic, but a
  silently substituted value that can hide a wrong result.

When one is used, three obligations attach:

- A trailing `// OK: ...` comment justifying why the call is acceptable:
  - `// OK: <specific reason>`: document the real precondition, invariant, or domain reason.
    Preferred whenever the reason isn't self-evident.
  - `// OK: obvious`: the default is self-evident from context (e.g.
    `desc.lines().next().unwrap_or("")`, where an empty desc gives an empty title).
  - Bare `// OK` is not used (reads like a truncated comment). Abbreviations (e.g. `SE`) are
    not used because they require a decoder ring for readers seeing the code out of context.
- **Alert the user in conversation** when introducing one, so the site gets reviewed and
  appropriate uses are learned. Don't let it ride in silently on a larger diff.
- For `.unwrap()` / `.expect(...)`, an `#[allow(...)]` at the site, because Rust projects
  enable the project-wide lints in `Cargo.toml`:

  ```toml
  [lints.clippy]
  unwrap_used = "warn"
  expect_used = "warn"
  ```

  Every panicking site is then opt-in and visible in the diff; clippy (in the per-commit flow)
  catches any that slip through. The `_or*` siblings have no clippy lint; they are covered by
  the comment convention and the conversational alert. (The vc-x1-work-repo-template's
  `CargoRust.toml` seeds a base `Cargo.toml` with this section already in place.)

```rust
let max = stderr_level.unwrap_or(LevelFilter::Info); // OK: default verbosity when -v/-vv absent
let first_line = desc.lines().next().unwrap_or("");  // OK: obvious

match matches.len() {
    1 => {
        #[allow(clippy::unwrap_used)]
        // OK: `1 =>` arm guarantees matches.len() == 1
        Ok(TitleMatch::One(matches.into_iter().next().unwrap()))
    }
    // ...
}
```

Tests (`#[cfg(test)]`) are exempt, since panicking on setup failure is the correct test
behavior.

1	//! The `sync` subcommand: fetch + classify + rebase / fast-forward
2	//! a workspace's repos against their remotes, then reposition `@`
3	//! onto the synced bookmark.
4	//!
5	//! `--bookmark` names a **work-repo** bookmark only: the bot
6	//! repo is a linear journal on `main` by design, so every
7	//! per-repo step (tracking preflight, classify, act, reposition)
8	//! resolves its bookmark via `repo_bookmark`, which pins the
9	//! bot repo to `main`.
10	//!
11	//! Sync is a single atomic operation — verify-then-act happens
12	//! inside one invocation against one fetch snapshot (a separate
13	//! check-then-apply pair of runs would race the remote). The

38	/// Fetch and sync a set of repos to their remotes.
39	///
40	/// One atomic operation: fetch, classify, fast-forward / rebase the
41	/// bookmark as needed, then reposition `@` onto it. On any failure
42	/// the starting state of every repo is restored via `jj op restore`.
43	///
44	/// Repo set is resolved from `-R/--repo` + `--scope`:
45	///
46	/// - `-R PATH` — workspace root, or a single repo to sync alone.
47	/// - `--scope=work|bot|work,bot` — keyword role selection,
48	///   resolved via the workspace root's `.vc-config.toml`.
49	/// - Neither — workspace-default scope:
50	///   - dual workspace (`.vc-config.toml` with `bot`) → `work,bot`
51	///   - single-repo workspace (`.vc-config.toml`, no `bot`) → `work`
52	///   - POR (no `.vc-config.toml`) → cwd

177	/// Resolve a `-R`/`--scope` pair into a concrete repo list.
178	///
179	/// `-R` and `--scope` compose:
180	///
181	/// - neither — workspace-default scope against the discovered root.
182	/// - `-R PATH` alone — just that repo.
183	/// - `-s ROLES` alone — roles against the discovered workspace root.
184	/// - `-R PATH -s ROLES` — roles against `PATH` as the workspace root.
185	///
186	/// `pub(crate)` — shared by `sync` and `revert`, which must resolve
187	/// the same invocation shape to the same repos.
188	pub(crate) fn resolve_repos(
189	    repo: &Option<PathBuf>,
190	    scope: &Option<Scope>,
191	) -> Result<Vec<PathBuf>, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
192	    match (repo, scope) {
193	        (None, None) => {
194	            let root = find_workspace_root();
195	            scope_to_repos(&default_scope(root.as_deref()), root.as_deref())
196	        }
197	        (Some(p), None) => Ok(vec![p.clone()]),
198	        (None, Some(s)) => scope_to_repos(s, find_workspace_root().as_deref()),
199	        (Some(p), Some(s)) => scope_to_repos(s, Some(p)),
200	    }
201	}

227	/// CLI entry point for the `sync` subcommand.
228	///
229	/// Thin wrapper over `sync_repos` that resolves `--scope` into a
230	/// concrete repo list (falling back to the workspace-default
231	/// scope) and forwards the rest. Tests call `sync_repos` directly
232	/// with absolute fixture paths. `ctx` is unused today — present
233	/// for the uniform subcommand-layer signature.
234	///
235	/// When `--quiet` is set, the global log filter is temporarily
236	/// clamped to `Warn` for the duration of the call and restored on
237	/// return, so `info!` calls throughout sync (plus any
238	/// subprocess-stderr routed through `common::run`) go dark. Errors
239	/// still surface at `Warn` / `Error` so script callers don't lose
240	/// diagnostics.
241	pub fn sync(_ctx: &Context, params: &SyncParams) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
242	    let repos = resolve_repos(&params.repo, &params.scope)?;
243	    if params.quiet {
244	        let prev = log::max_level();
245	        log::set_max_level(LevelFilter::Warn);
246	        let result = sync_repos(&repos, params);
247	        log::set_max_level(prev);
248	        result
249	    } else {
250	        sync_repos(&repos, params)
251	    }
252	}

254	/// Sync the given repos against their remotes.
255	///
256	/// Orchestrates the full flow: pre-flight clean-check on every repo,
257	/// snapshot each repo's current op id (persisted to
258	/// `.vc-x1/sync-state.toml` per repo), then hand off to `run_plan`
259	/// for fetch + classify + act, then reposition `@`.
260	///
261	/// **Stop-on-error**: a failure leaves every repo exactly where the
262	/// failing step stopped so the user can inspect what happened —
263	/// nothing is auto-reverted. The error report names each repo's
264	/// pre-sync op id and points at `vc-x1 revert`, which consumes the
265	/// persisted snapshots. On full success the snapshots are cleared
266	/// (a stale file must not become a revert target later).
267	///
268	/// Paths may be relative (resolved against the process cwd) or
269	/// absolute. Tests use absolute tempdir paths to avoid cwd dependence
270	/// under parallel `cargo test`.
271	pub fn sync_repos(
272	    repos: &[PathBuf],
273	    params: &SyncParams,
274	) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
275	    debug!(
276	        "sync: enter (check={}, bookmark={}, remote={})",
277	        params.check, params.bookmark, params.remote
278	    );
279	
280	    // Preflight: verify bookmark tracking on every repo before any
281	    // fetch/rebase. Implements "Non-tracking-remote bookmark detection"
282	    // — design at:
283	    //   https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1/blob/main/notes/chores/chores-06.md#non-tracking-remote-bookmark-detection-design
284	    for repo in repos {
285	        let bookmark = repo_bookmark(repo, &params.bookmark);
286	        if bookmark != params.bookmark {
287	            info!(
288	                "{}: bot repo — syncing 'main' ('{}' is a work repo bookmark)",
289	                repo.display(),
290	                params.bookmark
291	            );
292	        }
293	        crate::common::verify_tracking(repo, bookmark)?;
294	    }
295	
296	    let mut snapshots: Vec<(PathBuf, String)> = Vec::new();
297	    for repo in repos {
298	        let op_id = current_op_id(repo)?;
299	        debug!("{}: op snapshot = {op_id}", repo.display());
300	        state::save(
301	            repo,
302	            &op_id,
303	            repo_bookmark(repo, &params.bookmark),
304	            &params.remote,
305	        )?;
306	        snapshots.push((repo.clone(), op_id));
307	    }
308	
309	    // Run the plan, then reposition `@` onto the freshly-synced
310	    // bookmark (skipped in deprecated verify-only mode). Both live
311	    // inside the same stop-on-error region: any failure falls
312	    // through to the report below with state left in place.
313	    let result = run_plan(&snapshots, params).and_then(|()| {
314	        if !params.check {
315	            for (repo, _) in &snapshots {
316	                reposition_at(repo, repo_bookmark(repo, &params.bookmark), params)?;
317	            }
318	        }
319	        Ok(())
320	    });
321	
322	    if let Err(e) = &result {
323	        warn!("sync failed: {e}");
324	        warn!("stopping — state left as-is for inspection (no auto-revert)");
325	        warn!("pre-sync op snapshot per repo:");
326	        for (repo, op_id) in &snapshots {
327	            warn!("  {}: op {op_id}", repo.display());
328	        }
329	        warn!("undo with `vc-x1 revert`, or per repo: jj op restore <op> -R <repo>");
330	        debug!("sync: exit");
331	        return result;
332	    }
333	
334	    // Full success — the snapshots are no longer revert targets.
335	    for (repo, _) in &snapshots {
336	        state::clear(repo)?;
337	    }
338	
339	    debug!("sync: exit");
340	    Ok(())
341	}

343	/// Clean-case summary tail ("<N> repo(s) …" prefixed at the emit
344	/// site). Shared with main.rs's `long_about` so the documented
345	/// output shape can't drift from the emitted one.

348	/// Fetch and classify each repo, then act (or not, in verify-only).
349	///
350	/// Returns `Err` on the first failure so the caller can stop and
351	/// report; partial progress across repos is left in place for
352	/// inspection (see `sync_repos`).
353	fn run_plan(
354	    snapshots: &[(PathBuf, String)],
355	    params: &SyncParams,
356	) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
357	    // Phase 1 — fetch + classify silently.
358	    //
359	    // Each repo's fetch stderr is captured (rather than streamed to
360	    // `info!` via `common::run`) so we can decide after classification
361	    // whether to surface it. `jj git fetch`'s routine "Nothing
362	    // changed." chatter is the main thing we're suppressing here —
363	    // if nothing needs action, the user shouldn't see it.
364	    let mut fetched: Vec<(PathBuf, Vec<String>)> = Vec::new();
365	    let mut ctxs: Vec<RepoCtx> = Vec::new();
366	    for (repo, op_id) in snapshots {
367	        let lines = fetch_silent(repo, &params.remote)?;
368	        fetched.push((repo.clone(), lines));
369	        let state = classify(repo, repo_bookmark(repo, &params.bookmark), &params.remote)?;
370	        ctxs.push(RepoCtx {
371	            path: repo.clone(),
372	            op_id: op_id.clone(),
373	            state,
374	        });
375	    }
376	
377	    let any_action_needed = ctxs
378	        .iter()
379	        .any(|c| matches!(c.state, State::Behind { .. } | State::Diverged { .. }));
380	
381	    // Phase 2 — emit status. `--quiet` is enforced globally via the
382	    // log-level clamp in `sync()`, so these `info!` calls are already
383	    // suppressed in scripts; we just shape the output here.
384	    if !any_action_needed {
385	        let n = ctxs.len();
386	        let noun = if n == 1 { "repo is" } else { "repos are" };
387	        info!("sync: {n} {noun} {UP_TO_DATE_MSG}");
388	    } else {
389	        for (repo, lines) in &fetched {
390	            info!("{}: fetch {}", repo.display(), params.remote);
391	            for line in lines {
392	                info!("{line}");
393	            }
394	        }
395	        for ctx in &ctxs {
396	            log_state(&ctx.path, &ctx.state);
397	        }
398	    }
399	
400	    // Phase 3 — act (subprocess output streams through as usual).
401	    // `act_on_state` short-circuits in deprecated verify-only mode,
402	    // making it a true no-op here. Repositioning `@` onto the synced
403	    // bookmark happens after `run_plan` returns (see `sync_repos`),
404	    // outside the revert region.
405	    for ctx in &ctxs {
406	        act_on_state(ctx, params)?;
407	    }
408	
409	    // Phase 4 — verify-only mode is fatal when action would be
410	    // needed. The normal sync ran the action above and is done.
411	    if params.check && any_action_needed {
412	        let n_action = ctxs
413	            .iter()
414	            .filter(|c| matches!(c.state, State::Behind { .. } | State::Diverged { .. }))
415	            .count();
416	        let noun = if n_action == 1 { "repo" } else { "repos" };
417	        return Err(format!(
418	            "sync: {n_action} {noun} need action (see above) — \
419	             resolve with `vc-x1 sync` and re-run"
420	        )
421	        .into());
422	    }
423	    Ok(())
424	}

478	/// Reposition the bot repo's `@` onto `main`.
479	///
480	/// The session (`.claude`) repo is a linear journal on `main`, and its
481	/// `@` normally carries live session writes:
482	///
483	/// - `@-` already the `main` tip → no-op: `@` is where it belongs,
484	///   live writes stay in the working copy. (An unconditional
485	///   `jj new main` here would churn an empty `@`'s chid/op every
486	///   sync, or strand a non-empty `@`'s live writes — and any ochid
487	///   captured against its chid — on a sibling head.)
488	/// - Errors when `@-` isn't on `main` (not an ancestor-or-equal of the
489	///   bookmark) — refuse rather than guess.
490	/// - Otherwise `main` moved: `jj new main` starts a fresh `@` on the
491	///   bookmark; the prior `@` becomes a sibling head, which is
492	///   expected for the journal. A conflict is very unlikely given
493	///   `.claude`'s content; if one ever appears the user resolves it.
494	fn reposition_bot(repo: &Path) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
495	    let parent = jj::cid_short_of(repo, "@-")?;
496	    let tip = jj::cid_short_of(repo, "main")?;
497	    if parent == tip {
498	        debug!("{}: @ already on 'main'", repo.display());
499	        return Ok(());
500	    }
501	    if !jj::matches(repo, &format!("{parent}::main"))? {
502	        return Err(format!(
503	            "{}: @- ({parent}) is not on main — refusing to reposition @",
504	            repo.display()
505	        )
506	        .into());
507	    }
508	    info!("{}: jj new main", repo.display());
509	    run(
510	        "jj",
511	        &["new", "main", "-R", &repo_str(repo)],
512	        Path::new("."),
513	    )?;
514	    Ok(())
515	}

517	/// Reposition the work repo's `@` onto the synced `bookmark`.
518	///
519	/// Let `@-` be the parent of `@`:
520	///
521	/// - `bookmark == @-` → already positioned; no-op.
522	/// - `bookmark` a proper descendant of `@-`, `@` empty →
523	///   `jj new bookmark` (jj auto-abandons the old empty `@`).
524	/// - `bookmark` a proper descendant of `@-`, `@` non-empty → rebase
525	///   `@` onto `bookmark`, but only with `rebase` set (else prompt on a
526	///   TTY; skip + inform when declined or not a TTY).
527	/// - `bookmark` not a descendant of `@-` (diverged / `@` ahead) →
528	///   leave `@` and inform why it didn't move.
529	fn reposition_work(
530	    repo: &Path,
531	    bookmark: &str,
532	    rebase: bool,
533	) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
534	    let parent = jj::cid_short_of(repo, "@-")?;
535	    let tip = jj::cid_short_of(repo, bookmark)?;
536	    if tip == parent {
537	        debug!("{}: @ already on '{bookmark}'", repo.display());
538	        return Ok(());
539	    }
540	    if !jj::matches(repo, &format!("{parent}::{tip}"))? {
541	        info!(
542	            "{}: @- ({parent}) is not behind '{bookmark}' ({tip}); leaving @ in place",
543	            repo.display()
544	        );
545	        return Ok(());
546	    }
547	    // `bookmark` is a proper descendant of `@-` — safe to move a clean `@`.
548	    if at_is_empty(repo)? {
549	        info!("{}: jj new {bookmark}", repo.display());
550	        run(
551	            "jj",
552	            &["new", bookmark, "-R", &repo_str(repo)],
553	            Path::new("."),
554	        )?;
555	        return Ok(());
556	    }
557	    // `@` carries changes: rebase only on opt-in / confirmation.
558	    if !rebase && !confirm_rebase(repo)? {
559	        info!(
560	            "{}: @ has changes; left in place (pass --rebase to rebase onto '{bookmark}')",
561	            repo.display()
562	        );
563	        return Ok(());
564	    }
565	    info!("{}: rebasing @ onto '{bookmark}'", repo.display());
566	    run(
567	        "jj",
568	        &["rebase", "-b", "@", "-d", bookmark, "-R", &repo_str(repo)],
569	        Path::new("."),
570	    )?;
571	    if has_conflicts(repo)? {
572	        return Err(format!(
573	            "{}: rebase of @ onto '{bookmark}' produced conflicts",
574	            repo.display()
575	        )
576	        .into());
577	    }
578	    Ok(())
579	}

608	/// deprecated verify-only mode).

610	/// - `UpToDate` / `Ahead` / `NoRemote` → no-op (and no output, the state
611	///   was already logged by `log_state`).

613	/// - `Diverged` → `jj rebase -b <b> -d <b>@<remote>`, then probe
614	///   `conflicts()`. A non-empty result means the rebase produced
615	///   conflicted commits; return `Err` so the outer revert restores the
616	///   pre-fetch state.
617	fn act_on_state(ctx: &RepoCtx, params: &SyncParams) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
618	    let repo = &ctx.path;
619	    let bookmark = repo_bookmark(repo, &params.bookmark);
620	    let remote_rev = format!("{}@{}", bookmark, params.remote);
621	    match &ctx.state {
622	        State::UpToDate | State::Ahead { .. } | State::NoRemote => Ok(()),
623	        State::Behind { .. } => {
624	            if !params.check {
625	                info!("{}: setting '{bookmark}' to {remote_rev}", repo.display());
626	                jj::bookmark_set(repo, bookmark, &remote_rev)?;
627	            }
628	            Ok(())

630	        State::Diverged { local, remote } => {
631	            if !params.check {
632	                // `local` is either a single commit id or a comma-joined list
633	                // of heads when the bookmark is conflicted. Pick the head
634	                // that isn't the remote — that's the local-only tip. The
635	                // comma-joined path covers the jj post-fetch divergence
636	                // shape (local bookmark conflicted between old local head
637	                // and freshly-fetched remote head).
638	                let local_head = local
639	                    .split(',')
640	                    .find(|h| *h != remote)
641	                    .unwrap_or(local.as_str());
642	                info!(
643	                    "{}: rebasing {local_head} onto {remote_rev}",
644	                    repo.display()
645	                );
646	                run(
647	                    "jj",
648	                    &[
649	                        "rebase",
650	                        "-b",
651	                        local_head,
652	                        "-d",
653	                        &remote_rev,
654	                        "-R",
655	                        &repo_str(repo),
656	                    ],
657	                    Path::new("."),
658	                )?;
659	                if has_conflicts(repo)? {
660	                    return Err(format!("{}: rebase produced conflicts", repo.display()).into());

725	/// Classify the relationship between `bookmark` and `bookmark@remote`.
726	///
727	/// Uses `bookmarks(<b>)` rather than the bare name so a conflicted
728	/// bookmark (jj's representation of a diverged fetch) resolves to all
729	/// of its heads instead of erroring. When the set has multiple heads,
730	/// the bookmark is conflicted and the repo is `Diverged` by definition.
731	/// Otherwise we compare the single local head against the single
732	/// remote commit via two revset-ancestry probes.
733	///
734	/// Returns `NoRemote` when `<b>@<remote>` does not resolve — the caller
735	/// logs a skip and moves on.
736	fn classify(
737	    repo: &Path,
738	    bookmark: &str,
739	    remote: &str,
740	) -> Result<State, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
741	    let local_heads = local_bookmark_heads(repo, bookmark)?;
742	    let remote_rev = format!("{bookmark}@{remote}");
743	    let Some(remote) = try_commit_id(repo, &remote_rev)? else {
744	        return Ok(State::NoRemote);
745	    };
746	    if local_heads.is_empty() {
747	        return Err(format!("{}: bookmark '{bookmark}' does not exist", repo.display()).into());
748	    }
749	    if local_heads.len() > 1 {
750	        // Conflicted bookmark — jj's shape for post-fetch divergence.
751	        let local = local_heads.join(",");
752	        return Ok(State::Diverged { local, remote });
753	    }
754	    let local = local_heads.into_iter().next().unwrap(); // OK: `len() > 1` arm handled above, `is_empty()` handled above
755	    if local == remote {
756	        return Ok(State::UpToDate);
757	    }
758	    let local_is_anc = jj::matches(repo, &format!("{local}::{remote_rev}"))?;
759	    let remote_is_anc = jj::matches(repo, &format!("{remote_rev}::{local}"))?;
760	    Ok(match (local_is_anc, remote_is_anc) {
761	        (true, _) => State::Behind { local, remote },
762	        (false, true) => State::Ahead { local, remote },
763	        (false, false) => State::Diverged { local, remote },
764	    })
765	}

784	/// failure".

788	        Ok(id) => Ok(Some(id)),
789	        Err(e) if jj::is_no_such_revision(e.as_ref()) => Ok(None),
790	        Err(e) => Err(e),

1	//! `SubcommandRunner` trait
2	//!
3	//! The purpose is to simplify invoking a subcommand so `main`
4	//! can invoke any subcommand with one line:
5	//!
6	//! `Commands::Chid(args) => args.dispatch(&ctx),`
7	//!
8	//! Instead of the ~11 lines that the default `dispatch` below
9	//! now encapsulates.
10	//!
11	//! Implementors provide:
12	//!
13	//! - [`SubcommandRunner::to_params`] — build the clap-free
14	//!   `Params` from the clap `Args` (covers both `From` /
15	//!   `TryFrom` shapes uniformly via `Result<_, String>`).
16	//! - [`SubcommandRunner::run`] — the subcommand body.
17	//!
18	//! The default [`SubcommandRunner::dispatch`] builds `Params`
19	//! via `to_params`, runs via `run`, and maps the result to
20	//! `ExitCode`. Errors at any stage log via `error!` and return
21	//! `ExitCode::FAILURE`. `Context` is loaded once in `main` and
22	//! passed in by reference so a single `Context` is shared across
23	//! the (one) match arm that actually runs.
24	//!
25	//! ## See also
26	//!
27	//! - The wider CLI-args / subcommand-layer split this trait
28	//!   formalizes: [`ARCHITECTURE.md > args → Context + Params`][arch].
29	//! - Cycle design, ladder, evaluation gate:
30	//!   [`chores-10.md > 0.50.0-0`][open].
31	//! - Worked example, trait-shape decisions, naming:
32	//!   [`chores-10.md > 0.50.0-1`][port].
33	//! - First implementor: [`crate::chid`].
34	//!
35	//! [arch]: https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md#args--context--params
36	//! [open]: https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1/blob/main/notes/chores/chores-10.md#chore-open-subcommand-trait-sweep-0500-0
37	//! [port]: https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1/blob/main/notes/chores/chores-10.md#refactor-subcommandrunner-trait--chid-0500-1

39	use std::process::ExitCode;
40	
41	use log::error;
42	
43	use crate::context::Context;
44	
45	/// Trait implemented by every subcommand's clap `Args` type so
46	/// `main.rs` can dispatch via a single `args.dispatch(&ctx)`
47	/// call.
48	pub trait SubcommandRunner {
49	    /// The clap-free `Params` struct the subcommand body
50	    /// consumes.
51	    type Params;
52	
53	    /// Build `Params` from `Args`. `Result<_, String>` absorbs
54	    /// both `From` (return `Ok(...)`) and `TryFrom` (forward
55	    /// the error) shapes uniformly.
56	    fn to_params(&self) -> Result<Self::Params, String>;
57	
58	    /// Run the subcommand body.
59	    fn run(ctx: &Context, params: &Self::Params) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>;
60	
61	    /// Default dispatch: build `Params` via `to_params`, bracket
62	    /// the run with `crate::bm_track` enter/exit, execute via
63	    /// `run`, and map the result to `ExitCode`. Errors at any
64	    /// stage log via `error!` and return `ExitCode::FAILURE`.
65	    /// `bm_track` itself emits at `debug!`, so default runs stay
66	    /// quiet — no per-call gate is needed here.
67	    fn dispatch(&self, ctx: &Context) -> ExitCode {
68	        let params = match self.to_params() {
69	            Ok(p) => p,
70	            Err(e) => {
71	                error!("{e}");
72	                return ExitCode::FAILURE;
73	            }
74	        };
75	
76	        // Command name is the first positional after the binary;
77	        // clap has already validated it by the time we reach
78	        // dispatch (top-level parse errors exit earlier).
79	        let command_name = std::env::args().nth(1).unwrap_or_else(|| "?".to_string()); // OK: default when somehow invoked without a subcommand
80	
81	        crate::bm_track("enter", &command_name);
82	        let exit_code = match Self::run(ctx, &params) {
83	            Ok(()) => ExitCode::SUCCESS,
84	            Err(e) => {
85	                error!("{e}");
86	                ExitCode::FAILURE
87	            }
88	        };
89	        crate::bm_track("exit ", &command_name);
90	        exit_code
91	    }
92	}

##### 0.78.0-7 refactor: context-owned repo sessions

`Context` grows the session map the `-6` review designed:
lazily-opened `RepoSession`s keyed by canonicalized repo path,
opened on first use by `Context::session` and reused for the
rest of the invocation. Has-a, never is-a: an invocation
touches 0..N repos, and a repo-less `version` never opens one.
The five verbs move from facade fns onto `RepoSession` as
methods; the facade keeps one-shot wrappers for context-less
callers.

- `SubcommandRunner::run` (and `dispatch`) take
  `&mut Context`: the sessions are exclusive mutable state,
  and the borrow checker enforcing one live session borrow at
  a time is what a `RefCell` would trade for runtime panics.
  The fifteen non-consumer subcommands change signature only.
- Verbs as `RepoSession` methods: `commit`, `describe`,
  `bookmark_set`, `git_push_bookmark`, `git_fetch`, plus the
  `one_commit` resolver and `complete_newline`.
  `DebugCallback` goes private to the session module.
- One-shot wrappers stay for the context-less callers:
  fix-desc (`describe`), init (`bookmark_set`,
  `git_push_bookmark`), repo_utils (`commit`, `describe`).
  `git_fetch`'s only caller is sync, context-ful, so its
  wrapper is deleted rather than kept unused.
- `RepoSession::snapshot` now reloads at the op-store head
  for every repo, not only colocated ones: a session outlives
  single verbs in a `Context`, and a spawned `jj` (squash,
  new, rebase, op restore) may commit operations between
  verbs. Reuse skips only the open (settings + workspace
  load); freshness is per-verb, unchanged.
- Consumers: push threads `ctx` through `mutate` and the four
  mutating stages, and its `squash-push-bot` stage passes the
  same `ctx` into squash-push, so one bot-repo session serves
  the whole run; squash-push and sync take `ctx` for their
  verb sites (`fetch_silent`, `act_on_state`). Reads stay
  one-shot facade fns.
- Tests: `test_helpers::test_ctx()` builds a
  default-user-config `Context`; the push / sync /
  squash-push integration tests pass a fresh one per op call,
  matching the production one-context-per-invocation shape.

**What landed** (`0.78.0-7 refactor: context-owned repo sessions`, per the design settled at the `-6` review):

- **`Context` owns the sessions** (`src/context.rs`): a private `HashMap<PathBuf, RepoSession>` keyed by canonicalized repo path, opened lazily by `Context::session(&mut self, repo)` and reused for the rest of the invocation.
